description: This file contains shell script compatibility wrappers for the UCI (Unified Configuration Interface) system used in OpenWrt. It defines functions to load, set, revert, toggle, add, remove, and commit configuration options via the /sbin/uci command, facilitating interaction with UCI configurations programmatically in shell scripts.

methods.name: uci_load
methods.description: Loads the configuration data for a specified package using the uci command and evaluates the exported data.

methods.name: uci_set_default
methods.description: Ensures the specified package has a default configuration by importing and committing if not already set.

methods.name: uci_revert_state
methods.description: Reverts the configuration state for a specific package, section, and option.

methods.name: uci_set_state
methods.description: Sets a specific configuration option to a value within the state directory.

methods.name: uci_toggle_state
methods.description: Reverts and then sets a configuration option to toggle its state.

methods.name: uci_set
methods.description: Sets a configuration option to a value.

methods.name: uci_add_list
methods.description: Adds a value to a list-type configuration option.

methods.name: uci_get_state
methods.description: Retrieves a configuration value from the state directory.

methods.name: uci_get
methods.description: Retrieves a configuration value, optionally from a specified state directory, with a default fallback.

methods.name: uci_add
methods.description: Adds a new configuration section or sets a section type.

methods.name: uci_rename
methods.description: Renames a configuration option or section.

methods.name: uci_remove
methods.description: Removes a configuration option or section.

methods.name: uci_remove_list
methods.description: Removes a specific list item from a configuration list.

methods.name: uci_revert
methods.description: Reverts changes to a configuration option or section.

methods.name: uci_commit
methods.description: Commits the configuration changes for a specified package.
